summary: @whalent/agent-core ships obfuscated remote-control agent with PTY, WebSocket, SSH, and self-upgrade
details: Package's main entry and bin (`dist/index.cjs`, ~13.7 MB, invoked as `whalent-core`) is a heavily obfuscator.io-packed bundle (rotating string array `a0_0x41ac` of 106,679 entries, decoder `a0_0x14b6`, control-flow flattening, hex-renamed identifiers) that ships and imports `ws` (WebSocket client and server), `node-pty`, `ssh2`, `socks-client`, and `basic-ftp`. Bundle strings include remote-control tokens (`remote`, `upgrade`, `agent`, `endpoint`, `Authorization`, `token`) and loopback references to 127.0.0.1:3389 (RDP), 127.0.0.1:5900, and 127.0.0.1:5901 (VNC). The README describes the package as being 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades,' i.e. the running code is swapped by a remote party. The composition (network-arriving bytes fed into a PTY on the installer host, SSH/SOCKS pivoting primitives, and remote code replacement) is a remote-shell / remote-administration agent, and the full-entrypoint obfuscation conceals the C2 destination so the actual control endpoint cannot be identified from the shipped bytes.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
